items.title: uv version leaves lock file out-of-date
items.reason: Historical inverse of the new failure: changing only `pyproject.toml` left `uv.lock` stale; it led to the lock-and-sync behavior that now exposes the non-transactional error path.

items.title: make `uv version` lock and sync
items.reason: Introduced the current `uv version` lock/sync flow and explicitly documented that a non-noop set under `--locked` errors, but its implementation writes `pyproject.toml` before validation and has no revert path.

items.title: uv sync --locked --no-install-project fails if only project version changes
items.reason: Maintainer discussion confirms that a project-version change intentionally makes the lockfile out of date under `--locked`; unlike the new report, it concerns an externally changed file rather than `uv version` retaining its own edit after failure.

related.search_scope: Literal and exact-error searches covered `uv version`, `--locked`, `UV_LOCKED`, `pyproject.toml`, `lock_and_sync`, and “The lockfile ... needs to be updated.” Conceptual searches covered atomicity, rollback/revert, failed commands leaving project metadata changed, version-bump lock/sync behavior, and prior fixes. Open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests were searched. astral-sh/uv#15286 was inspected as a plausible candidate but ruled out because it requests avoiding or reducing full resolution/sync during version bumps rather than restoring files after a failed operation.

type_reason: Current source confirms a correctness defect: `uv version` writes the new `pyproject.toml` in `update_project` before `lock_and_sync` runs, and an error from locked validation propagates without restoring the file. The `--locked` rejection itself is intended, but retaining the command's partial edit is not. No existing issue or open pull request was found that tracks this same rollback failure.
summary: No duplicate was found. astral-sh/uv#13254 and its merged fix astral-sh/uv#13317 established that `uv version` must keep `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` synchronized, while astral-sh/uv#15643 confirms a version change should fail locked validation; the newly reported bug is the missing rollback after that expected failure.
draft_response: Thanks, this is a bug. The `--locked` error is expected because changing a static project version makes the lockfile out of date, but `uv version` should not retain its `pyproject.toml` edit after that validation fails. The current implementation writes the file before `lock_and_sync` and propagates the error without restoring it. astral-sh/uv#13254 and astral-sh/uv#13317 explain why the command updates the lockfile, but they do not cover rollback on failure. The next step is an integration regression test asserting that both `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` remain unchanged after `uv version --bump minor --locked`, followed by making the version edit use the same snapshot-and-revert behavior as other project-editing commands.
